To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a self-supervised hyperspectral classification framework can be developed for weed detection in crops using an autonomous mobile vehicle; (2) the framework can be extended to include prior knowledge about seeding pattern; (3) the framework can provide accurate classification of weeds in corn crops, with an overall accuracy of 95.3% and an average accuracy per class of 96.5% in a single pass over a 10 row corn crop.
A self-supervised weed detection system for hyperspectral imaging has been proposed and tested in a corn field.
we have developed and evaluated a self-supervised weed classification system for hyperspectral imaging that is capable of adapting to changes in environmental conditions and plant appearance.

the following questions: 1) What is the best approach to crop/weed discrimination using hyperspectral imaging in the context of an autonomous mobile vehicle? 2) How can we leverage prior knowledge about seeding pattern to provide an adaptive training method for hyperspectral crop and weed discrimination?
